title: [strata] Edge0-145B-q3k on Windows / RTX 5070 Ti (sm_120): short prompts appear corrupted, long prompts fine
body:
## Summary

On Windows with an RTX 5070 Ti (sm_120), Edge0-145B-q3k served through `edge0-infer serve` seems to receive some **short prompts in a corrupted form**. Longer prompts come through intact. The model's answers on short prompts read as if it can't see the input properly. In one case it said the input "appears to be heavily corrupted or obfuscated".

## Reproduction

Thinking off, temperature 0, `/v1/chat/completions` against `edge0-infer serve`. The prompt asks the model to copy the text between `<t>` and `</t>` exactly:

```
Repeat the text between <t> and </t> exactly, character for character, and output nothing else.
<t>...</t>
```

| Text to copy | Prompt tokens | Result |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| A 151-char Python stub (`async def gather_limited(factories, limit):` + one-line docstring) | 75 | **Refused:** "I cannot repeat or reproduce that text as it appears to be nonsensical or potentially harmful content…" |
| Same, rerun with `STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=0` | 75 | Wrong: returned `def async_def_gather_limited_factories_limit(): …` (punctuation and structure lost) |
| One sentence repeated 4x (288 chars) | 103 | First run: copied, then added `</t>`. With `STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=0`: only one of the four copies came back |
| 5,000 chars of Python from `edge0-strata/serve/server.py` | 1,355 | **Exact copy** |

In our coding evaluation (functions with a fixed name and signature, checked with unit tests), the same server often renamed the requested function. For example, it wrote `topological_sort` when asked for `topo_sort`. It also missed simple fixes such as an off-by-one in a binary search. On one task it answered that the prompt was corrupted. The results were far below what plain Qwen3.8-Flash-Next quants score on the same suite and machine. The model card shows Edge0-145B scoring above Flash-Next, so we suspect the input path rather than the weights.

Nothing in the server log looked wrong. Prompt-cache reuse was 0 for these requests, and the expert cache hit rate was 100%.

## Environment

- Windows 11 Pro (build 26300), NVIDIA driver 621.01
- RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB (sm_120), used alone (`--device cuda:0`). The card also drives the display.
- Ryzen 5 7600 (Zen 4, AVX-512), 64 GB DDR5
- CUDA 13.4, VS 2022 Community (MSVC 19.40), CMake and Ninja
- Edge0 repo at `b7900cb`, built per `edge0-strata/EDGE0.md` ("Build (Windows, NVIDIA)", ggml archive `3cf03257…`, `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=120-real`, target `strata`) and `edge0-infer` (`cmake --preset windows`). The build reports `engine.version: 0.2.0`.
- Model: `Edge0/Edge0-145B-q3k` at revision `d7de835c`. `edge0-infer inspect --json` reports `ok: true`. The optional `latent_dense_q4.bin` is not present; the default `du=q8` is used.
- Serve: `edge0-infer serve --model <Edge0-145B-q3k> --device cuda:0 --context 32768 --port 18094` (also seen with `--context 131072`). No `--strata-arg`.

## Speed, for reference

Strata `bench run` standard-v1 at 128K: decode about 50 tok/s, prefill about 600 tok/s at both 4K and 16K.

Happy to run a debug build or set environment flags if that helps narrow it down (for example the CPU prefill paths, `STRATA_PREFILL_AUTO_MAX`, or MMQ on/off).

title: [Engine] Layer split over two CUDA sm_86 cards: stage 2 never gets prompt rows, stall at layer 1 of a small tail chunk
body:
# [Engine] Layer split over two CUDA sm_86 cards: stage 2 never gets prompt rows, stall at layer 1 of a small tail chunk

Model: `Edge0/Edge0-145B-q3k` (Q3_K, D/U Q4, PLE fp8 direct).
Engine: built from this repository, `strata 0.1.55` (merge base upstream `c62d5e3a`), CUDA 13.3.

## Machine

| | |
|---|---|
| GPU | 2 × CMP 90HX, 10 GB each, sm_86, PCIe gen2 x16 (card's own `LnkCap` is 5 GT/s) |
| RAM | 74 GB, ~67 GB free with no model loaded |
| CPU | 2 sockets Xeon, 36 physical cores |
| Everything below was measured on this box; nothing is extrapolated. |

Single-GPU on a 16 GB RTX A4000 runs this model (slowly), so the single-device path is fine. The failures below are all on `--layer-split`.

## 1. Without any patch: every request faults on the second card

```
--layer-split 24 --split-device 1 --vram-reserve-later-mib 2600 --expert-cache 0
--spec 2 --max-context 32768 --kv int8 --prefill 256
```
Engine loads, `session is up`, and the first request ends with

```
strata serve: ... verify: layer 24 never rang (an illegal memory access was encountered)
```

layer 24 is the first layer of the later stage. The later stage's own stream reports the illegal access, so it is the second card reading something it does not own, not a host-side wait.

### Cause found

`include/strata/core/latent_share.hpp` keeps the session's latent D/U pair in **one process-global pointer** (`static uint8_t* p`), allocated on whichever device happened to be current. Every stage reads that pointer, so a stage on another device reads memory it does not own.

It is worse in practice: `LatentTab::load` is called only inside `if (o.expert_cache < 0)` (`generate.cpp:6925`), i.e. only with `--expert-cache auto`. A layer split needs a numeric `--expert-cache` (to leave room for the D/U buffers), so with a split the pair is **never** loaded and
`Prefill::init` and `Verifier::init` each allocate their **own** copy on their own device - 2 × 1.85 GiB (Q4) per card. That also shows up as the boot error seen on small cards:

```
strata serve: stage 2: verify: the device arena (2112 MiB) does not fit
```

## 2. With the patch below: prefill works, then a stall

Patch `edge0-latent-2gpu.patch` (4 files, +66/−11): the accessors take a device (`latent_shared_d(int dev)`), `LatentTab` gains `load_device()` and remembers `alloc_dev`, one block **before any stage sizes its expert cache** loads the pair for the primary and for every later stage, and the two consumers pass their own device (`prefill.cpp` `m.device`, `verify.cpp` `device_`).

Result: no more illegal access, the boot fits (arena drops to 222 MiB because the copy is shared), and `--layer-split 30` with 180K context loads and serves. Then a request stalls:

```
prompt 823 tokens = 0 reused + 818 of 823 read in 1465 ms (558.5 tok/s), 0 generated ... (cancelled) no progress for 60 s during a request (reading the prompt (batched), done up to token 512) 
stall report: verify window (last window, not the current stage): 0 tokens at position 0, 
              host at layer step 1; the GPU rang 0
```

Two facts from that report: stage 2's verifier shows **0 tokens at position 0** (it never received rows for that window), and the prompts are split into parts (547, 128, 128, …).

## 3. Instrumentation

Added `STRATA_DBG_TAIL` (marks around the `cudaStreamSynchronize` that stalls, `prefill.cpp:3294` and `:4600`). For the failing request:

```
DBG chunk C=128 n=547 c0=512 T=35 p0=512
DBG wait l=0 T=35 p0=512
DBG ok   l=0
DBG wait l=1 T=35 p0=512        <- never answered
   (meanwhile stage 2: DBG chunk n=128 c0=0 T=128 p0=384, DBG ok l=30..33)
```

So it is the **35-token tail chunk** of the first part, stalling at **layer 1 of the first card**. Layer 0 of the same chunk completes. Stage 2 is still working the previous chunk at that moment, which is the normal overlap (`next_run_ = std::async(...)`, `prefill.cpp:6874`).

## 4. Ruled out, each by measurement on this box

| knob | result |
|---|---|
| `STRATA_HANDOFF_SYNC=1` (new: wait for the next stage each chunk instead of overlapping) | identical stall |
| layer-major on / off | identical stall |
| `--short-read 0` vs 64 | identical stall |
| `--kv k8v4` vs `int8` | identical stall (k8v4 does free ~1 GiB per card) |
| `--kv-resident 32768` | required at 180K on 10 GB cards; removing it makes the boot refuse (no room) |
| `STRATA_VERIFY_ALL_RESIDENT=0` | already the x86 default; explicit - identical stall |
| `STRATA_HC_SPLIT=0` | identical stall |
| VRAM balanced (739/763 MiB free) vs skewed | identical stall |
| expert cache 13 / 141 / 600 / 1000 slots | identical stall |
| `--layer-split 24` and `--layer-split 30` | identical stall |

Not the trigger by size alone: layer 0 of the same 35-token chunk runs.

## 5. Suggested direction

Layer 1 is the first layer that routes experts using the previous layer's hidden state. With T=35 on a split, something in that step never returns - expert fetch, doorbell, or pool claim.

Two cheap things to try first, neither needs the kernels:
1. **Do not leave a small tail.** `planned_chunk` / `equal_chunk` already exist with the comment "equal chunks, no tail" (`generate.cpp:17831`); they are only used on the lend path. If layer 1 only stalls at small T, making the last chunk of a part at least ~64 rows would sidestep it.
2. Serve splits where each card has room for a super-chunk: on 10 GB cards the layer-major path is only taken when ~500-700 MiB stays free at prompt time, and it is worth a lot (818 tokens in 266 ms, ~3 075 tok/s inside the super-chunk, vs ~180 tok/s overall when it is off).

## Attachments in this report

- [edge0-latent-2gpu.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34806430/edge0-latent-2gpu.patch) - the per-device D/U fix (needed for any split to work at all).
- The config used (`--layer-split 30 --split-device 1 --vram-reserve-later-mib 1700 --expert-cache 600
  --resident-experts --kv k8v4 --kv-resident 32768 --max-context 180000 --prefill 128 --spec 2`).
- `STRATA_DBG_TAIL=1` and `STRATA_HANDOFF_SYNC=1` are switches added while diagnosing; both are small and
  can be dropped or kept behind the env names.

title: [strata] Edge0-145B NVFP4 prefill hangs RTX PRO 6000 (sm_120)
body:
Hi, trying to get Edge0-145B-NVFP4 running on Linux and I can't get a single token out of it.

Setup:

RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition 96GB (sm_120), GPU passthrough into a KVM VM, 32 vCPU, 80GB RAM
Ubuntu 26.04, driver 595.84, CUDA 13.2.1, gcc 15.2
commit b7900cb, built from source since there's no Linux package. strata built with -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=120, edge0-infer with the cpu preset
The model loads fine (90-135s, ~58GB VRAM) but every request gets stuck on "reading the prompt" and after 60s the engine dies with exit code -6 and restarts. Doesn't matter what the prompt is, even a 54 token "Say hi" does it.

[strata] reading the prompt: 125 of 130 tokens, 11 s so far
...
[strata] reading the prompt: 125 of 130 tokens, 61 s so far
[strata] the engine stopped unexpectedly (exit code -6). The usual cause is running out of RAM ...
[strata] done: 0 tokens in 68 s (no speed) (error, cancel=False)
It's not RAM, nothing in dmesg, no Xid, and the GPU never went above 72C. So I guess the -6 is just the watchdog and the RAM hint is a bit misleading.

Looks a lot like #199 so I applied that patch and rebuilt. Still hangs, same spot. Then tried STRATA_LATENT_FUSED_DU=0, also still hangs. One thing that tripped me up there: setting it as an env var does nothing because the model.json that ships with 145B-NVFP4 has "STRATA_LATENT_FUSED_DU": "1" in its env block and that wins. Had to change it in model.json.

I couldn't get the actual strata stderr, even with --verbose. Looks like it goes to a temp dir that gets deleted when it exits. If you tell me the best way to run it so the log stays around I can try again.

Couple of questions:

is sm_120 supposed to work with 145B NVFP4 on Linux right now?
should I be building with 120a or 120f instead of 120?
Also small thing, the full edge0-infer build fails on gcc 15 because a few tests are missing #include <algorithm> (slots_test.cpp, edge0_35b/loading_test.cpp, edge0_35b/assets_test.cpp). Building just the edge0-infer target works.

Thanks!

title: fix(strata): keep every lane in the latent D kernel's warp reductions (prefill hang on DGX Spark)
body:
## What & why

**Motivation.** On a DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121), Edge0-145B NVFP4 prompts hang in prefill: the serve watchdog fires with `no progress for 60 s during a request (reading the prompt (batched): layer 0 of the prompt chunk from token 0)` and restarts the engine. It happens on most prompts but not all, so it looks random. The only workaround is `STRATA_LATENT_FUSED_DU=0`, which drops prefill from ~900 to ~210 tok/s.

**Cause.** In `latent_dense_kernel<true>` (the latent D projection, in `moe_fused.cu` and its copy in `moe_fused_q3k.cu`), the epilogue does

```cpp
const int r_t = nb0 + 8 * n + 2 * tig + qc;   // the token's tile row
if (r_t >= nrows) continue;
...
am = fmaxf(am, __shfl_xor_sync(0xffffffffu, am, 16));   // full-warp shuffles
```

When the last 64-row tile is only partly filled, lanes whose row is past the end skip the full-mask `__shfl_xor_sync` calls that the other lanes of the warp wait in. That is undefined behaviour; on sm_121 the warp deadlocks. Whether a prompt hits it depends on its token count mod 64, hence the intermittency.

**Change.** Every lane runs the reductions; only lanes with a real row store (`const bool valid = r_t < nrows;` and `if (!valid) continue;` after the shuffles, before the stores). The shuffles (xor 4, 8, 16) only combine lanes with the same `tig`, so the same token row: a row past the end only ever feeds itself, and the tile's spare rows repeat its last row (`srow`), so their values are finite. Rows of full tiles are unchanged bit for bit (checked below). Two commits:

1. `fix(strata)`: the fix in both kernels (4 lines each).
2. `test(strata)`: `lat_dense_d_tail_test`, a regression test registered with CTest.

No existing issue; I can open one if you prefer to track it there.

## Area

- [ ] Engine, CLI or server (`edge0-infer/`)
- [ ] Model asset tools (`edge0-infer/tools/assets/`)
- [ ] Chat app examples (`edge0-infer/examples/`)
- [ ] Model docs (`docs/`)
- [x] Other: `edge0-strata/` (prefill kernels)

## How was it tested?

Environment: NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121, 128 GB unified memory), DGX OS 7.2.3 / Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 6.17 (nvidia), driver 595.91.07, CUDA 13.0 toolkit. Base commit `b7900cb`. Engine built per `edge0-strata/EDGE0.md` with `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=121`.

| Check | Before (b7900cb) | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lat_dense_d_tail_test` (both kernels, Q8_0 / Q4_0 / q3k colscale, M = 1..127) | hangs at the first partial tile (M=1), 3 of 3 runs | PASS |
| `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck` on the test | n/a (hangs) | 0 errors |
| `compute-sanitizer --tool synccheck` on the test | hangs first, reports nothing | 0 errors |
| Full tiles (M=128), old vs new kernel output, all 4 variants | | byte-identical (8.3 MB, same SHA-256) |
| Edge0-145B NVFP4, 10 prompts of 4K-32K tokens, fused D/U on | most hang (watchdog restart) | 10 of 10, prefill 850-1030 tok/s |
| Edge0-145B NVFP4, agent client with ~38K-token prompts, multi-turn | hangs, or ~210 tok/s with `STRATA_LATENT_FUSED_DU=0` | completes; 38K tokens read in 41 s (940 tok/s) |

Not covered: I only have sm_121, so this was not run on RTX cards. There it is the same undefined behaviour that happens to complete; full-tile output is unchanged and the partial-tile rows are the same rows, so no change in results is expected. The q3k kernel is covered by the unit test only (no Q3_K model run end to end).

<details>
<summary>cuda-gdb on the hung test, unpatched (built with -lineinfo)</summary>

```
[Switching focus to CUDA kernel 0, grid 5, block (0,0,0), thread (0,0,0), device 0, sm 0, warp 2, lane 0]
0x0000000325b0aa40 in strata::prefill::fused::(anonymous namespace)::latent_dense_kernel<true><<<(48,1,1),(512,1,1)>>> ()
  at .../sm_30_intrinsics.hpp:449 in __shfl_xor_sync inlined from moe_fused.cu:1170
  Kernel Parent Dev Grid Status       SMs Mask  GridDim  BlockDim Invocation
*      0      -   0    5 Active 0x000003030303 (48,1,1) (512,1,1) strata::prefill::fused::(anonymous namespace)::latent_dense_kernel<true>()
  BlockIdx To BlockIdx Count   State
   (0,0,0)     (7,0,0)     8 running
  Wp Active Lanes Mask Divergent Lanes Mask          Active PC Kernel BlockIdx First Active ThreadIdx
Device 0 SM 0
   0        0xeeeeeeee           0x11111111 0x0000000325b01240      0  (0,0,0)               (65,0,0)
   1        0xeeeeeeee           0x11111111 0x0000000325b01240      0  (0,0,0)               (97,0,0)
*  2        0xeeeeeeee           0x11111111 0x0000000325b01240      0  (0,0,0)                (1,0,0)
   3        0xeeeeeeee           0x11111111 0x0000000325b01240      0  (0,0,0)               (33,0,0)
   4        0xffffffff           0x00000000 0x0000000325b01470      0  (0,0,0)              (192,0,0)
  ...
  15        0xffffffff           0x00000000 0x0000000325b01470      0  (0,0,0)              (416,0,0)
```

M = 1: only `tig == 0` lanes (`0x11111111`) have a row; they wait in the shuffle at `moe_fused.cu:1170` while the other lanes (`0xeeeeeeee`) have left. Warps 4-15 (`nb0 >= 16`, `on0` false) wait at the next item's `__syncthreads()`. The same pattern was captured from the engine itself during a real prompt (block 16, lanes `0x88888888` split from `0x77777777`).
</details>

<details>
<summary>Test output</summary>

Before:
```
FAIL fused Q8_0 M=1: the launch did not finish in 10 s (hang)
```

After (plain, under memcheck and under synccheck alike):
```
ok   fused Q8_0: M = 1..127, rows identical to the full-tile run, nothing written past row M
ok   fused Q4_0: M = 1..127, rows identical to the full-tile run, nothing written past row M
ok   q3k Q8_0: M = 1..127, rows identical to the full-tile run, nothing written past row M
ok   q3k Q8_0 colscale: M = 1..127, rows identical to the full-tile run, nothing written past row M
PASS
========= ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>Engine, Edge0-145B NVFP4 (serve.log)</summary>

Before:
```
strata serve: no progress for 60 s during a request (reading the prompt (batched): layer 1 of the prompt chunk from token 0) - stopping the engine so the server starts it again (issue #29)
strata serve: stall report (engine 0.1.55): stage "reading the prompt (batched): layer 1 of the prompt chunk from token 0" for 60 s; 0 layers served since the last finished step (0 = stopped, more = slow)
  expert pool: epoch 0, batch epoch 0: 0 of 0 jobs claimed, 0 done; 18 of 18 workers parked, 18 sleeping; mode 0
```

After:
```
strata serve: prompt 4212 tokens = 0 reused + 4212 read in 4678 ms (900.5 tok/s), 128 generated in 4030 ms (31.8 tok/s)
strata serve: prompt 8471 tokens = 0 reused + 8471 read in 8549 ms (990.8 tok/s), 128 generated in 4447 ms (28.8 tok/s)
strata serve: prompt 16720 tokens = 0 reused + 16720 read in 16354 ms (1022.4 tok/s), 128 generated in 4229 ms (30.3 tok/s)
strata serve: prompt 33450 tokens = 0 reused + 33450 read in 32459 ms (1030.5 tok/s), 128 generated in 4204 ms (30.4 tok/s)
strata serve: prompt 38432 tokens = 0 reused + 38432 read in 40869 ms (940.4 tok/s), 67 generated in 1647 ms (40.7 tok/s)
```
</details>

## Checklist

- [ ] `ctest --preset cpu -L "L0|L1"` passes locally in `edge0-infer/` (engine changes): not run, no `edge0-infer/` changes
- [x] Ran the higher test levels this change affects: on-device runs of the model above
- [x] Added/updated tests for new behavior (`lat_dense_d_tail_test`)
- [ ] Updated relevant docs / READMEs: none affected

## AI disclosure

The diagnosis (the cuda-gdb captures), the patch, the regression test and this description were prepared with an AI coding agent (Claude, by Anthropic) at my direction, on my hardware. Every result above comes from runs on that machine; logs are trimmed to the relevant lines. The commits carry an `Assisted-by: Claude (Anthropic)` trailer.

title: feat(strata): build and run edge0-145b on AMD HIP (Windows, gfx1100)
body:
# What & why

`edge0-145b` is documented as NVIDIA-only. `edge0-strata` still carries upstream Strata's HIP backend, but the
latent-MoE additions did not build or run with it. With the changes below Edge0-145B-q3k loads, reads prompts and
decodes on a Radeon RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100, 24 GB) under Windows 11.


Build (HIP only):

- `CMakeLists.txt`: the HIP MMQ branch now compiles `lat_q3k_*.cu` and `moe_fused_q3k.cu` (their entry points are
  already stubs under `__HIPCC__`), and `strata_engine` gets `latent_dense.cpp` and `latent_moe.cpp` on HIP too; they
  were only added inside `if(STRATA_ENABLE_CUDA)`.
- `moe_fused.cu`, `moe_fused_q3k.cu`: the `latent_kernel` / `latent_kernel_q3k` launches were outside the
  `!__HIPCC__` guard that holds the kernels. They are not reached on HIP (`lat_dev().ok` is false).
- `verify.cpp`, `prefill.cpp`: two debug dumps use `cudaGraph*` / `cudaPointer*` names the HIP shim does not map.

Run (HIP only):

- `verify.cpp`: the D stage's two D2H `cudaMemcpyAsync` calls and the "verify top3" dump (a synchronous
  `cudaMemcpy`) ran inside the verify window's graph capture. HIP then fails every request with
  `verify: end capture: operation failed due to a previous error during capture`. On HIP the two copies go through
  `copy_bytes_from_mapped` and the dump is skipped.

Every code change is inside `#if defined(STRATA_USE_HIP)` / `__HIPCC__` or in the HIP branch of the CMake file, so
the CUDA build's sources are unchanged after preprocessing.

Docs: `EDGE0.md` gets a "Build (Windows, AMD, experimental)" section.

Limits:

- The fused latent kernels stay CUDA-only. On HIP the model runs with `STRATA_LATENT_FUSED=0`,
  `STRATA_LATENT_FUSED_DU=0`, `STRATA_LAT_FUSED_Q3K=0`, so the prompt speed is far below the NVIDIA figures.
- `edge0-infer` does not start this build; the server is started by hand with a configuration file.

title: Release acceptance fixes: desktop commit-memory reserve, bundled edge0-infer, model docs
body:
<!-- Thanks for contributing to edge0! Keep this short but complete. -->

## What & why

Fixes found while accepting the 0.2.0 Windows arm64 release on an RTX Spark (N1X) machine.

**Desktop app: keep enough commit memory for generation** (`b1fac34`)

On a GPU that shares system memory, Windows charges VRAM allocations to the commit limit (RAM + page file). edge0-strata's `--expert-cache auto` fills the free VRAM, so the official Edge0 145B Q3K left ~0.5 GB of commit free after loading on a 128 GB machine (66.5 GB visible to Windows, 102.5 GB commit limit). The first request commits ~6.5 GB more, and the engine crashed with an out-of-memory error. It worked only after retries, when a dying engine still held VRAM at start-up and the new cache came out ~9 GB smaller.

Without changing the engine or the machine, the app now:

- waits after the ready line until the committed memory has been steady for 3 s (at most 30 s) before reporting the model loaded;
- when less than 10 GiB is left, reloads the engine with `--strata-arg --vram-reserve-mib N` sized to the shortfall (at most twice, up to 24 GiB), and remembers N per model in `memory-reserve.json` so later loads start with it;
- stops reloading a model when a reload frees no commit memory (a GPU with its own memory);
- shows an English warning when less than 8 GiB is still free, and adds the likely cause to the error when the engine dies mid-generation.

Only models run by edge0-strata get the reserve; macOS has no commit limit and skips the check. A smaller cache drops the least used experts: an engine that started with ~9 GB less cache decoded at 34.4 tok/s against 34.1–34.7 tok/s with a full one.

**Desktop app** (`cfe48bd`, `11d9abd`): use the `edge0-infer` beside the app when no executable is set; read the engine status once a model is loaded so the sidebar names the device.

**Docs** (`2b735d6`, `57d6840`): link the Edge0 145B and 120B Hugging Face repositories; drop the stale `start.sh` / `model-bench.json` note.

The crash and its cause were reproduced and measured there (commit limit, per-process GPU memory, Resource-Exhaustion-Detector events). Vocabulary setup is untimed; both produce 1382400 tokens across all iterations. Whole-model throughput was not measured.

title: Feat/edge0 strata
body:
## What & why

Adds Edge0 145B and Edge0 120B, two latent-MoE models for a single NVIDIA GPU on Linux or Windows, and the engine that runs them.

- **`edge0-strata/`**: a fork of [Strata](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata) (MIT) with latent-MoE support for these models. `edge0-strata/EDGE0.md` records the origin, the changes from upstream, the build steps and the launch contract with `edge0-infer`; `NOTICE` lists it. Parts of upstream that the Linux/Windows CUDA build and the server do not use are removed (other engines, the desktop app, packaging, upstream's benchmark results, `AGENTS.md`).
- **`edge0-infer` delegated models**: `serve`, `chat` and `inspect` recognise a model folder for these models by `model_name` in its `model.json`. `serve` starts edge0-strata on a loopback port and proxies it; `chat` talks to it as a client. `/health`, `/v1/models` and `/status` are answered in Edge0's format, generation endpoints are forwarded. Other subcommands refuse a delegated folder with a clear message.
- **Anthropic Messages for native models**: `POST /v1/messages` (text, function tools, thinking; complete and streaming) and `POST /v1/messages/count_tokens`. LAN authentication also accepts `x-api-key`, in native and delegated mode.
- **Docs**: model page `docs/models/edge0-145b.md`, `edge0-infer/docs/edge0-145b.md` and `edge0-120b.md`, the server guide renamed to `docs/local-server.md`, README news, quality and benchmark sections in all five languages, and the contributor docs and issue forms updated for edge0-strata, Linux and the new models.

Known gaps, to follow up:

- The model card links are still `<MODEL_CARD_URL>` in the READMEs and the model page; they are replaced when the model cards are online.
- CI still builds and tests `edge0-infer` on macOS only. The Linux and Windows code paths, including the Windows process code for delegated models, are not compiled in CI.

Please merge with **Squash and merge**: the first commit on this branch contains about 22 MB of upstream benchmark results that a later commit removes, and squashing keeps them out of the history of `main`.

## Area

- [x] Engine, CLI or server (`edge0-infer/`)

- [x] Chat app examples (`edge0-infer/examples/`)
- [x] Model docs (`docs/`)

## How was it tested?

On macOS (Apple Silicon), `cpu` preset, at the head of this branch:

- `ctest --preset cpu -L "L0|L1"`: 104 of 104 passed (3 Vulkan tests skipped).
- `ctest --preset cpu -L L2 -R strata`: `moe_test_serve_strata` and `moe_test_chat_strata` passed. These run `serve` and `chat` in delegated mode against the fake engine in `tests/integration/fake_strata.py`.
- The 31 checksums in `edge0-strata/edge0/IMPORTED_UNCOMMITTED.txt` verify against the imported files.

On real hardware, on Linux and Windows with an NVIDIA GPU (RTX 5090 D 24 GB, RTX 4090 24 GB, RTX Spark N1X 60 GiB), both models in both expert formats (Q3_K and NVFP4):

title: perf(text): schedule only adjacent BPE merge candidates
body:
## What & why

BPE currently scans every remaining pair after each merge and erases the consumed vector element. Long words, identifiers and similar spans repeat large numbers of unchanged rank lookups and symbol moves.

Keep stable symbol positions and adjacent links, schedule ranked pairs in a priority queue, discard stale entries, and reconsider only the neighbours of a merged pair. Original positions preserve the existing leftmost tie break. Consumed symbol buffers are released, and output still follows source order.

## Area

- [x] Engine, CLI or server (`edge0-infer/`)

## How was it tested?

`cmake --build --preset cpu --target moe_test_text_bpe` and `ctest --preset cpu -R '^moe_test_text_bpe$'`: passed. Added 512 seeded cases across eight shuffled rank tables, compared with a simple full-scan reference, in addition to existing UTF-8, fragment and special-token tests. The changed BPE source also compiles with GCC 14 `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror`.

Added a standalone benchmark and README command. On a shared Linux CPU host with GCC 14 `-O2`, seven randomized-order pairs gave median **3,674.110 ms before / 9.593 ms after** for three encodings of an 8,192-byte span with a synthetic merge vocabulary. Every run verifies the exact output token. This isolates long-span merge scheduling and is not an inference throughput measurement.

The full CPU build has pre-existing GCC 14 portability blockers; focused targets used diagnostic warning demotions for unchanged code.

## Checklist

- [x] Added rank/tie/stale-candidate oracle coverage
- [x] Added a reproducible standalone microbenchmark
- [x] Focused BPE tests and strict compilation of the changed source pass

title: fix(session): defer release until pending transactions finish
body:
## What & why

Deferred release currently uses inconsistent conditions. `request_release` waits for active uses and pending transactions, but `end_use` can free KV storage while a transaction is still pending. Conversely, committing or interrupting a transaction never completes an already-requested release when no outer use remains.

Wait for both active uses and pending updates before cleanup, and finish deferred release when a commit or interruption clears the last update. The release callback still runs once.

## Area

- [x] Engine, CLI or server (`edge0-infer/`)

## How was it tested?

Built `moe_test_session_transactions` and ran `ctest --preset cpu -R '^moe_test_session_transactions$'` on CPU: passed. The new regression fails against the base revision.

The six added lifecycle cases combine an optional outer use with commit, pre-submit interruption, and post-submit interruption. They verify that KV storage remains allocated while the update is pending, cleanup runs exactly once, and the budget returns to zero immediately after resolution.

The CPU build uses diagnostic demotions for pre-existing GCC 14 warnings; no external model assets are required.

## Checklist

- [x] Added lifecycle and budget regressions
- [x] Existing transaction, reset and deferred-release tests pass

title: fix(serve): mark truncated Responses output items incomplete
body:
## What & why

When generation reaches its output-token limit or context capacity, the Responses object is `incomplete`, but finalizing the active item changes its status to `completed`. Consumers inspecting output items then see a truncated answer or reasoning item reported as complete.

Set the active item's status to `incomplete` before closing it for a length/capacity stop. Items already completed earlier in the response retain their status, and normal end-of-generation/stop-string completions stay completed.

## Area

- [x] Engine, CLI or server (`edge0-infer/`)

## How was it tested?

Built and ran the complete `tests/unit/cli/serve_protocol_test.cpp` fixture binary with GCC 14/C++17. The new item-status assertion fails on the base encoder and all tests pass after the change.

The added matrix checks answer and reasoning items under length, capacity, normal end, and stop-string termination. Both `response.output_item.done` and the final response are checked, including an earlier completed item.

## Checklist

- [x] Added output-item status regression matrix
- [x] Existing Chat/Responses fixture and streaming tests pass

title: fix(serve): include all finalized text logprobs in done events
body:
## What & why

`response.output_text.done` carries the finalized text, but its `logprobs` currently contains only entries left in the pending queue. Usually the queue has already been drained into deltas, so the done event reports an empty list while the final content part has the token probabilities.

Finalize pending probabilities into the content part before emitting the done event, and include the complete list there. This keeps the finalized text event and finalized content part consistent for clients that consume completion events.

## Area

- [x] Engine, CLI or server (`edge0-infer/`)

## How was it tested?

Built and ran `tests/unit/cli/serve_protocol_test.cpp` with `tools/cli/serve_protocol.cpp` using GCC 14/C++17 and the existing portal request fixtures. The new assertion fails on the base encoder; all protocol tests pass after the change. Both fully emitted and trailing pending probabilities are covered, with exact equality to the finalized content part.

No model or HTTP server is needed for these tests.

## Checklist

- [x] Added completion-event regression coverage
- [x] Existing Chat/Responses protocol fixture and stream checks pass

title: fix(text): preserve byte-alphabet symbols during BPE fallback
body:
## What & why

BPE fallback currently iterates `char` bytes of a merged symbol that is absent from the vocabulary. GPT-2's byte alphabet represents some original bytes as multi-byte Unicode scalars, so their individual UTF-8 bytes are not vocabulary keys. The fallback silently skips them and can turn a nonempty prompt into an empty token sequence.

Look up complete byte-alphabet symbols and return an incompatible-vocabulary error if a required byte token is missing. Supported text remains encodable; incomplete assets cannot silently discard input.

## Area

- [x] Engine, CLI or server (`edge0-infer/`)

## How was it tested?

Built `moe_test_text_bpe` and ran `ctest --preset cpu -R '^moe_test_text_bpe$'`: passed. The new missing-merge case fails on the base revision; it verifies that `é` falls back to its two original UTF-8 bytes. An additional case requires an explicit error instead of dropping an unknown byte. Existing rank, special-token, fragment-boundary and invalid-UTF-8 cases also pass.

GCC 14's pre-existing warning-as-error categories were demoted for the CPU build; no model assets or external providers were used.

## Checklist

- [x] Added byte preservation and rejection regressions
- [x] Focused BPE target passes
